correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the exact (C,L) one-step transitions, including the loss of a leaf when its original-tree parent gets any new child. Their centered combination \(D_n=L_n-pC_n/(1+p)\) has drift \(-D_n/n\) and exact squared-increment formula, yielding \(\mathbb E D_n^2=p(2-p)\mathbb E C_n/((1+p)^2(p+2))\) for all \(n\ge3\). Yule birth embedding gives an a.s. positive component-size limit, an L² martingale/Kronecker argument gives a.s. leaf proportion, and a predictable quadratic-variation calculation plus bounded-increment martingale CLT yields the mixed Gaussian limit. The standalone package checker has 313 passing exact full-state and tree-enumeration assertions; simulation is explicitly diagnostic, not proof. Residual risk: asymptotic Gaussian argument relies on standard stable martingale CLT hypotheses, which are individually checked in the proof.

value.rationale: The source separately treats the root cluster size and global leaf-colour observables, but whether a vertex is an original-tree terminal vertex is a natural structural characteristic of the root-connected cluster. The result supplies a complete a.s. composition law and a surprisingly exact finite residual variance, plus a self-normalized CLT despite random sublinear cluster size. This cannot be inferred from either marginal statistic; it distinguishes original terminality from new leaves created by edge deletion and provides a sharp second-order description of the retained root population. The case \(p=1\) correctly specializes to the classical recursive-tree leaf variance, while \(p<1\) has a nondegenerate random Gaussian scale.
